2026年10月19日、CAFCは、Google v. Valtrus Innovations事件において、発明者の供述を裏付ける独立した証拠として、Microsoft
Wordによって自動生成されたメタデータ（metadata）を認め、さらに、出願準備期間中の発明者及び代理人の行為が合理的に継続した勤勉性（reasonably continuous diligence）の要件を満たすとした特許審判部（PTAB）の判断を支持した。
本事件は、2013年3月16日の米国特許法改正（AIA）施行以前の、いわゆる先発明主義（First-to-Invent）に基づく事件である。
これに対し、Valtrusは、Bushee特許の出願日より前に本件発明を着想しており、さらに、その後704特許の出願に至るまで合理的に継続した勤勉性を示していたとして、Bushee特許を先行技術から除外すべきであると主張した。
PTABはValtrusの主張を認め、Bushee特許は本件において先行技術に該当しないと判断した。その結果、Googleは対象クレームの進歩性欠如を立証できなかった。Googleは、このPTABの判断を不服としてCAFCに控訴した。
Googleは、発明開示書類及びそのメタデータは発明者自身の管理下にあったものであり、発明者の供述を裏付ける独立した証拠とはいえないと主張した。しかし、CAFCは、この主張を退けた。
CAFCは、Microsoft Wordによって自動生成されるメタデータは、発明者自身が記述した文章とは性質が異なることを指摘した。特に、Wordファイルに記録された作成者情報やタイムスタンプは、発明者の供述する発明の着想日と整合していた。

# Patent Evidence in Microsoft Word Metadata Saves Google
...
A WORD FILE'S HIDDEN METADATA JUST SAVED A PATENT FROM GOOGLE. YOUR ENGINEERS ARE CREATING THIS KIND OF EVIDENCE EVERY DAY On October 19, the Federal Circuit decided Google v. Valtrus Innovations in a precedential opinion by Judge Cunningham. Google had challenged all 23 claims of US Patent 6,728,704, on merging search results from multiple search engines, in an IPR. Its lead reference had been filed on July 24, 2001, about five weeks before the patent's own filing date. Valtrus answered that its inventor had conceived the invention earlier, and the Board agreed. The court affirmed. The interesting part is the proof. An inventor's own testimony about when he had an idea is not enough; it needs independent corroboration, and unwitnessed notebooks or emails do not count on their own. Here the corroboration was the author and date metadata that Microsoft Word generated automatically for the inventor's invention disclosure. ***Google LLC v. Valtrus Innovations Ltd.*, No. 2024-1945 (Fed. Cir. Oct. 19, 2026)**

In our Case of the Week, the Federal Circuit affirmed a Patent Trial and Appeal Board decision ruling that Google failed to prove claims 1–23 of U.S. Patent No. 6,728,704 unpatentable. That patent, which dates back to 2001, was filed under the pre-AIA statutory structure, under which an inventor could get around prior art by establishing that they had conceived the patent before the prior art date, and diligently reduced the invention to practice thereafter.  But the Federal Circuit has cautioned that attempts to antedate a prior art reference must be corroborated.  At issue here was a decision concerning whether the patentee successfully corroborated prior conception and reduction to practice.  The Federal Circuit held that automatically generated Microsoft Word metadata can independently corroborate an inventor’s testimony of early conception under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. § 102(e).

The ’704 patent, owned by Valtrus, claims methods and computer-readable memory for merging search-result lists from multiple search engines. Google petitioned for *inter partes* review, asserting that prior art combinations involving U.S. Patent No. 6,711,569 (the “Bushee” patent), filed July 24, 2001, would have rendered the ‘704 patent claims, filed August 27, 2001, obvious. In response, Valtrus sought to antedate Bushee under pre-AIA § 102(e) by demonstrating that one of its co-inventors conceived of the claimed search-engine list-merging invention before Bushee’s July 24 filing date. The Board ruled in favor of Valtrus, concluding that the co-inventor’s earlier conception date was corroborated by Word documents and their metadata showing authorship and timestamps. Accordingly, the Board concluded Bushee was not prior art.

On appeal, Google argued the Board’s factual findings on conception were not supported by substantial evidence.

Google disputed diligence only from August 8 to August 27, 2001, a period it described as about 11 business days (Op. 9). The court held that substantial evidence supported the Board.
